title: I am the bread of life (John 6:22–51)
hookLine: the first I AM: whoever comes to me will never hunger

cards: Next morning, the crowd from the hillside wakes up and Jesus is gone. So are the disciples. They grab whatever boats they can find and cross the lake to Capernaum looking for him.
When they find him, he doesn't say welcome. He says, gently but plainly: you're not here because of the signs. You're here because you ate the bread and were filled.
People come back to the place they last got fed. Who doesn't? Then he tells them what he's really offering.

teach.b: "Labour not for the meat which perisheth," he says: food that goes stale. Work for food that lasts.
The crowd brings up their history: "Our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat."
Manna fell every morning in the wilderness, enough for one day, never more. Can you top that? Jesus says the true bread from heaven isn't something Moses gave; it's something the Father gives now.
And the crowd, like the woman at the well asking for that water, says: "Lord, evermore give us this bread."
Then he says it: "I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst."

teach.h: THE FIRST OF SEVEN I AM SAYINGS.
teach.b: It's the first of seven great sayings in John where Jesus says I am and names a picture: bread, light, the door, the good shepherd, the resurrection, the way, the vine. We'll meet every one on this path.
Bread was the plainest thing on any table in that world, the food of every family, rich and poor. He doesn't say I am a feast, or a rare delicacy.

teach.h: I AM THE BREAD OF LIFE.
teach.b: He says I am bread: something you need daily, that keeps you alive. Christians understand this in different ways. Many hear it about faith: coming to Jesus feeds a hunger nothing else fills.
Catholic and Orthodox Christians, with many others, also hear the bread of communion. Many hear both at once. And the word he keeps returning to is life.

how: Christians often connect this saying with communion; in many churches, the bread is shared at the Lord's Supper, the Eucharist or Holy Communion, and many Christians also say grace before ordinary meals.

o: a rich feast kept for special holy days
the manna Moses gave, still falling each day
plain daily food: Jesus's picture of himself

bread, light, door, shepherd, resurrection, way, vine.

he says they came because they ate the bread and were filled.

games.q: you crossed the lake looking for the man who fed you. you mention the manna your ancestors ate. what does he say?
o: "I can give you even more manna."
games.why: "I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger." not a meal, but himself.

practice: If you have a piece of bread or a cracker nearby, take it; if not, picture one, and think of the field, the wheat, the person who baked it.
Take one small bite and chew slowly, longer than feels normal, noticing the simple fact of being fed.
Then ask what you're hungry for that bread can't fill: if you pray, bring that hunger to God, and if you don't, give thanks for the bread.

wordCard.voice: Bread. The everyday food Jesus named himself as, the first of his seven I am sayings in John: whoever comes to him will never hunger.

orig.note: Greek: bread, a loaf. The everyday food of every home in Jesus's world.

carryVoice: Your line: bread of life. Daily bread, plain and needed, not a rare feast. See you tomorrow.
